observation_summary: The StrBuilder.contains(char) and indexOf(char, int) methods were iterating over the entire underlying character array (thisBuf.length) instead of the active portion of the string (size), causing the methods to look beyond the end of the string.
reasoning_summary: The bug is a classic iteration strategy error. The loop condition was using the capacity of the buffer (thisBuf.length) rather than the actual number of characters stored (size). This is a procedural logic error in the implementation of the search algorithm, not a missing guard (Checking) or a simple initialization error (Assignment/Initialization).
evidence_used: The bug report states: 'StrBuilder contains usages of thisBuf.length when they should use size'
The fix diff shows the loop condition 'i < thisBuf.length' being changed to 'i < this.size' in both contains(char) and indexOf(char, int) methods.
The failing test error message: 'The contains(char) method is looking beyond the end of the string'

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix involves changing a loop condition, the root cause is not a missing validation or guard, but an incorrect iteration strategy that processes invalid data (the unused buffer space).
The issue is not about the initial value of a variable, but the logic of the loop termination condition.
